invariants.rationale: The method always returns a non-null List, either a new LinkedList or the original keys, so the result cannot be null.
The method contract guarantees the return value is a List, which matches the declared return type.
The deduplication process only removes duplicates, so the size of result cannot exceed the size of the input keys.
It is typical for parallelism in distributed processing to be set to a sensible value of 1 or above; negative or zero values would be illogical.
If the result is empty, it must be because the input was empty. Otherwise, at least one key would be present in the deduplicated result.
